chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhuwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mundal ibn Ali al-'Anazi, from Muhammad ibn Mutarrif, from Masma', from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali (peace be upon him). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When God, Blessed and Exalted, is angry with a nation but does not send down chastisement upon it, its prices rise, its lifespans are shortened, its merchants do not profit, its fruits do not ripen, its rivers are not bounteous, its rains are withheld from it, and its wicked people are set to rule over it.

key_terms.الْعَذَاب: Chastisement/punishment — direct divine punishment as distinct from the subtle signs described
key_terms.تبارك وتعالى: Blessed and Exalted — an honorific epithet for God emphasizing His transcendence and sanctity
key_terms.شِرَار: The wicked/evil ones — those of corrupt character who rise to power as a sign of collective divine displeasure
key_terms.غَضَب الله: Divine anger/wrath — God's displeasure manifesting through withdrawal of blessings

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of God's anger upon a nation according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam Ali (AS) from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), describes seven signs of divine displeasure toward a community that is not yet being directly punished. The signs are socioeconomic and environmental in nature: inflation, shortened lives, unprofitable trade, failed harvests, depleted rivers, drought, and the rise of corrupt rulers. This teaching was understood by the early Muslim community as a warning that divine wrath can manifest subtly through worldly deterioration before overt punishment descends, urging communities toward repentance and reform.
word_analysis: and are given power/set to rule
